Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 21, verses 1–4:

It is Meccan.

{1} This is an expression of wonder at the state of people: that reminder does not benefit them, that they do not heed a warner, and that their reckoning and recompense for their good and bad deeds have drawn near, while they are {in heedlessness, turning away}; that is, heedless of that for which they were created, and turning away from that with which they were restrained. It is as if they were created only for this world, and born only to enjoy it. And Allah, exalted is He, does not cease to renew reminder and admonition for them, and they do not cease in their heedlessness and turning away.

{2} For this reason He said: ﴿No reminder comes to them from their Lord, newly revealed﴾, reminding them of what benefits them and urging them toward it, and of what harms them and warning them against it. ﴿But they listen to it﴾, listening in a way that establishes the proof against them, ﴿while playing﴾.

{3} ﴿Their hearts distracted﴾; that is, their hearts are heedless, turning away, and absorbed in worldly aims, and their bodies are playing. They have occupied themselves with indulging in desires, practicing falsehood, and uttering vile speech, although what should be incumbent upon them is that they be other than this quality: their hearts should turn toward the command and prohibition of Allah, and listen to it in a way that grasps its intended meaning, and their limbs should strive in the worship of their Lord for which they were created. They should keep the Resurrection, the reckoning and the recompense in mind. By this their affairs are completed, their states are set right, and their deeds are purified. Regarding the meaning of His words ﴿The reckoning of people has drawn near for them﴾, there are two opinions:

The first: this community is the last of the nations, its Messenger is the last of the messengers, and the Hour will be established upon its community. Thus the reckoning has drawn near with respect to what came before it of the nations, based on the saying of the Prophet (ﷺ): "I and the Hour have been sent like these two," and he joined his index finger and the one next to it.

The second opinion: the intended meaning of the nearness of the reckoning is death, and that whoever dies, his resurrection is established and he enters the abode of recompense for deeds. This is an expression of wonder at every heedless, turning-away person who does not know when death will overtake him, in the morning or the evening. This is the state of all people, except those whom divine providence reaches, so that they prepare for death and what follows it.

Then He mentioned what the disbelieving wrongdoers confer about in secret, out of obstinacy and opposing truth with falsehood. They conferred and conspired among themselves to say about the Messenger (ﷺ): "He is merely a human being like you; so what has distinguished him over you and singled him out among you? If one of you claimed a claim like his, his statement would be of the same kind as his. But he wants to make himself superior over you and to lead you. So do not obey him or believe him. He is a sorcerer, and what he has brought of the Qur'an is sorcery. So turn away from him and make the people shun him, and say: ﴿Will you then approach magic while you see?﴾" This is said while they know that he is truly the Messenger of Allah, through the dazzling signs they witness, which others did not witness; but wretchedness, wrongdoing and obstinacy drove them to it.

{4} Allah, exalted is He, has encompassed in knowledge what they conferred about, and He will recompense them for it. For this reason He said: ﴿He said: My Lord knows the word﴾, the hidden and the manifest, ﴿in the heaven and the earth﴾; that is, in everything that their regions encompass. ﴿And He is the All-Hearing﴾, of all voices, with their varying languages and diverse needs. ﴿The All-Knowing﴾, of what is in the minds and what the inner hearts conceal.

{5} God mentions the slander of those who denied Muhammad ﷺ and what he brought of the Great Qur'an, and that they spoke about it, saying about it various false sayings. At another time they say: "He invented it, fabricated it, and forged it of his own accord." At another time they say: "He is a poet, and what he brought is poetry." Yet anyone with even the slightest acquaintance with the reality of the Messenger's condition, who considers what he brought, will be certain beyond any doubt that it is the most sublime and highest of speech, that it is from God, and that no human can produce anything like part of it. This is how God challenged His enemies to produce its like, despite their strong motives to oppose it and their enmity, yet they were unable to produce anything of its opposition, and they knew this. Otherwise, what was it that roused them, unsettled them, kept them sleepless, and left their tongues stammering, if not the truth against which nothing can stand? They say these things about it only because they did not believe in it, to repel those who did not know it. And it is the greatest of the continuous signs indicating the soundness of what the Messenger ﷺ brought and his truthfulness, and it is sufficient and a cure. Whoever seeks another proof besides it, or proposes a sign other than it, is ignorant and unjust, resembling those obstinate ones who denied him, and who asked for the proposed signs which were most harmful to them and in which they had no benefit. For if their aim was to know the truth once its proof is clear, then its proof has already become clear without them; and if their aim was to make him incapable and to establish an excuse for themselves in case he did not bring what they asked for, then they, in this state, even if the signs they requested were brought, would certainly not believe. Had every sign come to them, they would not believe until they saw the painful punishment. For this reason God said of them: {So let him bring us a sign, as the earlier ones were sent [with signs]}; i.e., like the she-camel of Salih, the staff of Musa, and the like.

{6} God said: {Not one town that We destroyed before them believed}; i.e., with these proposed signs. Indeed, His custom requires that whoever asks for them and then receives them, yet does not believe, will be hastened with punishment. The earlier peoples did not believe in them, so will these believe in them?! What distinguished them over those? And what good is in them that would require belief upon their presence? This interrogation carries the meaning of negation; i.e., such a thing will never come from them.

{7–9} This is an answer to the doubts of those who denied the Messenger, who said: "Why was he not an angel, one who needs no food or drink and does not walk about in the markets? And why was he not immortal? If he is not like that, it shows that he is not a messenger!" These doubts have persisted in the hearts of those who deny the messengers. They resembled one another in disbelief, so their statements resembled one another. Thus God, exalted is He, answered these doubts for these deniers of the Messenger, who acknowledge the existence of the messengers before him. Even if there were only Abraham, peace be upon him, whose prophethood all communities acknowledge, and the polytheists claim to follow his religion and creed, [the answer would be enough]: the messengers before Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, were all human beings who eat food and walk in the markets, and to whom human conditions befall, such as death and other things. God sent them to their peoples and nations; some believed them and some denied them. God made true for them what He promised them of deliverance and happiness for them and their followers, and He destroyed the transgressors who denied them. So why is it that the false doubts are raised against the denial of Muhammad's messengerhood, when they exist also in his fellow messengers, whom the deniers of Muhammad acknowledge? This is a most clear argument against them: if they acknowledge a messenger from among humans, and they will never acknowledge a messenger who is not human, then their doubts are false, and they have invalidated them by their own acknowledgment of their corruption and their self-contradiction.

Now, if their argument is extended to denying the prophethood of humans altogether, and to claiming that there cannot be a prophet unless he is an immortal angel who does not eat food, then God has answered this doubt by His saying: {They say, "Why has an angel not been sent down to him?" Had We sent down an angel, the matter would have been decided, and they would not be reprieved. And had We made him an angel, We would have made him a man, and We would have confused them about what they are confusing.} And [He answered that] humans have no capacity to receive revelation from the angels: {Say, "If there were angels walking securely on the earth, We would have sent down to them from the heaven an angel as a messenger."} So if you have doubt and lack knowledge about the state of the earlier messengers, then ask the people of remembrance (ahl al-dhikr) from the earlier scriptures, such as the People of the Torah and the Gospel, and they will inform you of what they possess of knowledge, and that they were all human beings of the same kind as those to whom they were sent.

Although the cause of this verse concerns asking about the state of the earlier messengers from the people of remembrance, who are the people of knowledge, it is general in every matter of religion, its fundamentals and its branches, when a person lacks knowledge of it: he should ask those who know it. In it is the command to learn and to ask the people of knowledge, and they were only commanded to ask them because it is obligatory upon them to teach and to answer with what they know.

In restricting the asking to the people of remembrance and knowledge, there is a prohibition against asking those known for ignorance and lack of knowledge, and a prohibition against them presuming to take on that role. And in this verse is evidence that there are no female prophets among women, neither Mary nor others, due to His saying: {except men}.

{10} That is: {Indeed We have sent down to you}, O you to whom Muhammad ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib was sent, {a Book}: glorious, and a clear Qur'an. {In it is your reminder}; that is, your honour, your pride and your elevation. If you remember through it what it contains of true reports and believe them, comply with the commands it contains, and avoid the prohibitions it contains, your standing will be raised and your affair will become great. {Will you not then understand?}: what benefits you and what harms you. How is it that you do not act upon what contains your reminder and your honour in this world and the Hereafter? Had you possessed intellect, you would have taken this path. Since you did not take it, and instead took other paths which bring about your lowliness and baseness in this world and the Hereafter, and your wretchedness in both, it becomes known that you have no sound intellect and no sound judgment.

This verse has been fulfilled in what has happened. Those who believed in the Messenger, and those among the Companions and those after them who were reminded by the Qur'an, attained an elevation, a towering exaltedness, a great renown, and a nobility above kings, which is well known to everyone. Likewise, it is known what befell those who did not raise their heads through this Qur'an, nor were guided by it or purified by it from hatred, lowliness, degradation and wretchedness. There is no path to the happiness of this world and the Hereafter except through remembrance of this Book.

**{21}** When Allah, exalted is He, explained the perfection of His power and greatness, and that everything submits to Him, He denounced the polytheists who took deities besides Allah from the earth, in utmost incapacity and lack of power. {Do they raise the dead?}: this is an interrogative used in the sense of negation; i.e., they are unable to raise them up and gather them. This is explained by His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And they have taken, besides Him, gods that create nothing, while they are themselves created, and they possess not for themselves any benefit or harm, nor [power over] death or life or resurrection﴾ [25:3], and ﴿They have taken besides Allah gods, that they may be helped. They are not able to help them, and they are [as] troops brought forth [for them]﴾ [36:74–75].

**{22}** The polytheist worships a creature that neither benefits nor harms, and abandons sincere devotion to Allah, to whom belongs all perfection, and in whose hand is the command, benefit and harm. This is from his lack of success, his misfortune, his abundant ignorance, and his severe wrongdoing. Indeed, existence is not set in order except upon one God, just as it came into being only by one Lord. Therefore He said: ﴿If there were in them [i.e., the heavens and the earth] gods other than Allah, they would have been ruined﴾: in their very essence, and whoever is in them of creatures would be corrupted.

The explanation of this: the upper and lower worlds, as seen, are in the most perfect state of righteousness and order, in which there is no defect, flaw, obstruction, or opposition. This indicates that its Manager is one, its Lord is one, and its God is one. For if it had two managers and two lords, or more than that, its order would be disrupted and its pillars would collapse. For they would contend and oppose one another: if one of them wished to direct a thing and the other wished its non-existence, then the existence of both their wills together is impossible, and the existence of the will of one to the exclusion of the other indicates the other's incapacity and lack of power. And their agreement upon one single will in all matters is not possible. Thus it is necessarily determined that the Dominant, whose will alone exists without any hinderer or opponent, is Allah, the One, the Subduer. Therefore Allah mentioned the proof of mutual contention in His saying: ﴿Allah has not taken a son, nor is there with Him any god; [if there were], then each god would have taken away what he created, and some of them would have overcome others. Exalted is Allah above what they describe﴾ [23:91]. And from it, according to one of the two interpretations, is His saying: ﴿Say: If there were with Him other gods, as they say, they would have sought a way to the Owner of the Throne﴾ [17:42], ﴿Glory be to Him, and exalted is He far above what they say, [with] great exaltedness﴾ [17:43].

Therefore He said here: ﴿Exalted is Allah﴾: i.e., He is transcendent and sanctified above every deficiency, by virtue of His perfection alone. ﴿Lord of the Throne﴾: which is the ceiling of creation, the widest and greatest of it. So His lordship over what is beneath it is all the more so. ﴿Above what they describe﴾: i.e., the deniers and disbelievers, [in attributing] the taking of a son and a consort, and that He should have a partner in any way whatsoever.

**{23}** ﴿He is not questioned about what He does﴾: due to His greatness, His might, and the perfection of His power, no one can hinder or oppose Him, neither by word nor by deed; and due to the perfection of His wisdom and His placing of things in their proper places, and the excellence of their perfection, which is the best that the intellect can conceive. Therefore no question is directed at Him, because His creation contains no defect or imperfection. ﴿And they will be questioned﴾: i.e., all the creatures, about their deeds and words, because of their incapacity and poverty, and because they are servants, whose actions and movements are determined. Thus they have no power of disposal or management, over themselves or over others, even to the weight of an atom.

**{24}** Then he returned to censuring the condition of the polytheists, who took deities besides Him. So say to them, rebuking and reproaching: ﴿Or have they taken besides Him gods? Say, "Produce your proof."﴾: i.e., your argument and evidence for the correctness of what you have gone to. They will not find any way to that; rather, conclusive proofs have been established for its falsehood. Therefore He said: ﴿This is the reminder of those with me and the reminder of those before me﴾: i.e., the scriptures and the laws agree on the correctness of what I told you concerning the refutation of polytheism. This is the Book of Allah, which contains the mention of everything with its rational and transmitted proofs, and these earlier books are all proofs and evidences for what I have said. Since it is known that the proof and demonstration were established against them regarding the falsehood of what they went to, it is known that they have no proof; for a decisive proof is one whose opposition is certainly absent, otherwise it would not be conclusive, and even if oppositions are found, they are doubts that avail nothing against the truth. And His saying: ﴿Rather, most of them do not know the truth﴾: i.e., they persisted in what they are upon only by imitating their predecessors, disputing without knowledge or guidance. Their not knowing the truth is not due to its obscurity or subtlety, but rather due to their turning away from it; otherwise, if they had given it the slightest attention, the truth would have become clear to them from falsehood with complete and manifest clarity. Therefore He said: ﴿So they are turning away﴾.

**{25}** When Allah, exalted is He, turned to mention the earlier ones, and commanded that they be referred to in explaining this matter, He explained it in the most complete explanation in His saying: ﴿And We did not send before you any messenger except that We revealed to him that there is no deity except Me, so worship Me﴾. Thus all the messengers before you, along with their books, have as the essence and foundation of their message the command to worship Allah alone, with no partner, and the explanation that He is the true God who is worthy of worship, and that worshipping anything other than Him is false.

They see the heavens and the earth and find them ﴿joined together﴾: the former has no clouds and no rain, and the latter is lifeless and dead, with no plants in it. ﴿Then We parted them﴾: the heaven with rain, and the earth with vegetation. Is that not evidence that He is the Truth, that all else is false, that He is the one who gives life to the dead, and that He is the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate? For this reason He said: ﴿Will they not then believe?﴾ That is: with sound belief, free of doubt and of association.

Then He enumerated the signs of the horizons, saying:

{31} That is: among the proofs of His power, perfection, oneness and mercy is that, since the earth would not be stable except through the mountains, He set them firm in it and pinned it down, lest it sway with its people; that is, lest it be agitated, so that the servants could not settle upon it, cultivate it, or remain established on it. He anchored it with mountains, and thereby there came about the benefits and advantages that have come about.

And since the mountains are connected to one another in a very extensive way, if they were left in their state as lofty peaks and towering summits, the connection between many lands would be cut off. So from the wisdom and mercy of God He placed between those mountains {fijājan subulan}, that is, easy paths, not rugged ones, {so that they may be guided} to reaching their objectives in the lands, and so that they may be guided, through reflecting upon this, to the oneness of the Bountiful Giver.

This applies to all the signs of the heaven: its height, its vastness, its greatness, its beautiful color, its wondrous perfection, and other sights within it, including the fixed stars and the wandering planets, and its sun and moon giving light, from which night and day arise, and their constant swimming in their orbits. Likewise the stars, by which the benefits of the servants are established, such as heat, cold and the seasons, and by which they know the reckoning of their worship and their dealings, rest at night, become calm and settled, and disperse by day to strive for their livelihoods. Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 21, verses 34–35:

{34} When the enemies of the Messenger were saying: ﴿Wait for him to be struck by the misfortunes of death﴾, Allah the Exalted said: This is a well-trodden path and a paved road. We did not grant any human before you, O Muhammad, eternal life in this world. So when you die, the way of those like you among the messengers, prophets and friends of Allah [and others] is the same. ﴿Then if you die, will they be the ones who abide forever?﴾ That is: If you die, will they live on after you? Let them then enjoy eternity, if it exists. But that is not the case; rather, ﴿everyone upon it will perish﴾.

{35} For this reason He said: ﴿Every soul will taste death﴾. This encompasses all the souls of creation, and that this is a cup that must be drunk, no matter how long a servant's span lasts and how many years he lives. But Allah the Exalted brought His servants into being in this world, commanded and forbade them, and tested them with good and evil, with wealth and poverty, with honor and humiliation, with life and death, as a trial from Him, the Exalted: ﴿that He may test you as to which of you is best in deed﴾, and who will be seduced at the places of temptation and who will be saved. Then ﴿to Us you will be returned﴾, and We will recompense you for your deeds: if good, then good, and if evil, then evil. ﴿And your Lord is not ever unjust to the servants﴾.

And this verse proves the falsehood of the view of those who claim that al-Khidr (al-Khidr, the figure associated with the story in Surat al-Kahf) remains alive and is eternal in this world. That is a claim for which there is no evidence, and it contradicts the legal texts (al-adillah al-shar'iyyah).

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 21, verses 36–41:

{36} This is from the extent of their disbelief. When the polytheists saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), they mocked him and said: ﴿Is this the one who mentions your gods?﴾ That is: this one who, in their estimation, is despised, who reviles your gods, disparages them and speaks ill of them. That is: do not pay attention to him, and do not give him any importance. This is their mockery and their contempt for him, on account of what is in fact part of his perfection. For he is the most complete and the most excellent, and among his virtues and noble qualities is the sincere devotion of worship to Allah, the censure of everything worshipped besides Him, the belittling of it, and the mention of its (true) station and status. But the true object of scorn and mockery is those disbelievers who have gathered every blameworthy character trait, and even if they had nothing but their disbelief in the Lord and their denial of His messengers, they would thereby become among the basest and most abject of creation. Despite this, their mention of the Most Merciful, which is the highest of their states, is itself disbelief on their part, because they do not mention Him or believe in Him except while they are polytheists. Thus their mention (of Him) is disbelief and polytheism, so how (then) are their other conditions? For this reason He said: ﴿And they, at the mention of the Most Merciful, are disbelievers.﴾ In the mention of His name, "the Most Merciful" here, there is a clarification of the ugliness of their condition, and of how they met the Most Merciful, the bestower of all blessings and the averter of calamities, from whom alone is every blessing the servants have and by whom alone evil is repelled, with disbelief and polytheism.

{37} ﴿Man was created of haste.﴾ That is: he was created hasty, hurrying toward things and seeking their occurrence quickly. Thus the believers hasten the punishment of Allah upon the disbelievers and are slow to bring it about, while the disbelievers turn away and seek the punishment hastily, out of denial and obstinacy, saying: ﴿When is this promise, if you are truthful?﴾ And Allah, exalted is He, gives respite and does not neglect, and is forbearing, and sets for them a determined term. ﴿When their term comes, they cannot delay it an hour, nor can they advance it.﴾ For this reason He said: ﴿I will show you My signs﴾; that is, in My retribution upon whoever disbelieved in Me and disobeyed Me. ﴿So do not ask Me to hasten it.﴾

{38} ﴿And they say, "When is this promise, if you are truthful?"﴾ They said this statement out of delusion, before the punishment had been justified against them and before the torment had descended upon them.

{39} If only ﴿those who disbelieved would know﴾ their dreadful state ﴿when they cannot keep the Fire off their faces nor off their backs﴾, since it will have encompassed them from every side and covered them from every place, ﴿nor will they be aided﴾; that is, no one else will help them, so they will be given no help, and they will not be able to help themselves.

{40} ﴿Rather, it will come upon them suddenly﴾ — the Fire — ﴿and will stun them﴾ with agitation, terror and great fear. ﴿They will not be able to repel it﴾, for they are too humbled and weak for that. ﴿Nor will they be granted respite﴾; that is, they will not be given time, so that the punishment is deferred for them. Had they known this state with true knowledge, they would not have hastened the punishment, and they would have feared it with the greatest fear, but when this knowledge departed from them, they said what they said.

{41} When He mentioned their mockery of His Messenger through their saying: ﴿Is this the one who mentions your gods?﴾, He consoled him by telling him that this is the practice of earlier nations with their messengers, so He said: ﴿And messengers before you were certainly mocked, but those who ridiculed them were beset by what they used to mock.﴾ That is: there descended upon them ﴿what they used to mock﴾; that is, the punishment descended upon them and the means (of salvation) were cut off from them. So let these people beware lest there befall them what befell those deniers.

Thus the believers hasten the punishment of Allah upon the disbelievers and are slow to bring it about, while the disbelievers turn away and seek the punishment hastily, out of denial and obstinacy, saying: ﴿When is this promise, if you are truthful?﴾ And Allah, exalted is He, gives respite and does not neglect, and is forbearing, and sets for them a determined term. ﴿When their term comes, they cannot delay it an hour, nor can they advance it.﴾ For this reason He said: ﴿I will show you My signs﴾; that is, in My retribution upon whoever disbelieved in Me and disobeyed Me. ﴿So do not ask Me to hasten it.﴾

{38} ﴿And they say, "When is this promise, if you are truthful?"﴾ They said this statement out of delusion, before the punishment had been justified against them and before the torment had descended upon them.

{39} If only ﴿those who disbelieved would know﴾ their dreadful state ﴿when they cannot keep the Fire off their faces nor off their backs﴾, since it will have encompassed them from every side and covered them from every place, ﴿nor will they be aided﴾; that is, no one else will help them, so they will be given no help, and they will not be able to help themselves.

{40} ﴿Rather, it will come upon them suddenly﴾ — the Fire — ﴿and will stun them﴾ with agitation, terror and great fear. ﴿They will not be able to repel it﴾, for they are too humbled and weak for that. ﴿Nor will they be granted respite﴾; that is, they will not be given time, so that the punishment is deferred for them. Had they known this state with true knowledge, they would not have hastened the punishment, and they would have feared it with the greatest fear, but when this knowledge departed from them, they said what they said.

{41} When He mentioned their mockery of His Messenger through their saying: ﴿Is this the one who mentions your gods?﴾, He consoled him by telling him that this is the practice of earlier nations with their messengers, so He said: ﴿And messengers before you were certainly mocked, but those who ridiculed them were beset by what they used to mock.﴾ That is: there descended upon them ﴿what they used to mock﴾; that is, the punishment descended upon them and the means (of salvation) were cut off from them. So let these people beware lest there befall them what befell those deniers.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 21, verses 36–41:

{36} This is from the extent of their disbelief. When the polytheists saw the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), they mocked him and said: ﴿Is this the one who mentions your gods?﴾ That is: this one who, in their estimation, is despised, who reviles your gods, disparages them and speaks ill of them. That is: do not pay attention to him, and do not give him any importance. This is their mockery and their contempt for him, on account of what is in fact part of his perfection. For he is the most complete and the most excellent, and among his virtues and noble qualities is the sincere devotion of worship to Allah, the censure of everything worshipped besides Him, the belittling of it, and the mention of its (true) station and status. But the true object of scorn and mockery is those disbelievers who have gathered every blameworthy character trait, and even if they had nothing but their disbelief in the Lord and their denial of His messengers, they would thereby become among the basest and most abject of creation. Despite this, their mention of the Most Merciful, which is the highest of their states, is itself disbelief on their part, because they do not mention Him or believe in Him except while they are polytheists. Thus their mention (of Him) is disbelief and polytheism, so how (then) are their other conditions? For this reason He said: ﴿And they, at the mention of the Most Merciful, are disbelievers.﴾ In the mention of His name, "the Most Merciful" here, there is a clarification of the ugliness of their condition, and of how they met the Most Merciful, the bestower of all blessings and the averter of calamities, from whom alone is every blessing the servants have and by whom alone evil is repelled, with disbelief and polytheism.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 21, verses 42–44:

{42} He, exalted is He, says, mentioning the helplessness of those who have taken other gods besides Him, and that they are in need of and compelled toward their Lord, the Most Merciful, whose mercy encompasses the righteous and the wicked in their night and their day. So He says: ﴿Say, "Who protects you by night and by day from the Most Merciful?"﴾; that is, who guards you and preserves you ﴿by night﴾ when you are asleep on your beds and your senses are gone, and ﴿by day﴾ at the time of your dispersal and heedlessness? ﴿From the Most Merciful﴾; that is, in place of Him, is there another? That is: can anyone preserve you besides Him? There is no guardian except Him. ﴿Rather, they are turning away from the remembrance of their Lord.﴾ Therefore they associated others with Him. Otherwise, if they had turned to the remembrance of their Lord and received His admonitions, they would have been guided to their right course and granted success in their affairs.

{43} ﴿Or do they have gods that can protect them from Us?﴾; that is, if We intend harm for them, is there among their gods one who can prevent them from that evil and calamity descending upon them? ﴿They cannot help themselves, nor will they be accompanied by Us.﴾; that is, they will not be aided in their affairs from Our side. And if they are not aided by Allah, then they are forsaken in their affairs, unable to bring any benefit or repel any harm.

{44} What made them persist in their disbelief and polytheism is His saying: ﴿Rather, We gave enjoyment to these and their fathers until life lengthened for them.﴾; that is, We provided them with wealth and children and lengthened their lives, so they became occupied with enjoying them and were distracted by them from that for which they were created. The term grew long for them, so their hearts hardened, their rebellion grew great, and their disbelief became severe. Had they turned their attention to those around them on the earth, right and left, they would have found only one destroyed, and they would have heard only the cry of a mourner, and they would have perceived only generations succeeding one another in destruction, and death has set up its snares in every path to hunt souls. For this reason He says: ﴿Do they not see that We come to the land, reducing it from its outskirts?﴾; that is, by the death of its people and their annihilation little by little, until Allah inherits the earth and whoever is upon it, and He is the Best of inheritors. Had they seen this condition, they would not have been deceived and persisted in what they are upon. ﴿Then are they the victors?﴾: those who are able to escape the decree of Allah and who have the power to prevent death? Is this their description, that they should be deceived by long life? Or, when the messenger of their Lord comes to seize their souls, do they submit and humble themselves, showing no slightest resistance at all?

{45} That is, {Say}: O Muhammad, to all of mankind: {I only warn you by revelation}; that is, I am only a messenger. I do not bring you anything of my own, nor do I have the treasures of God, nor do I know the unseen, nor do I say that I am an angel. I only warn you with what God has revealed to me. So if you respond, you have responded to God, and He will reward you for that; but if you turn away and oppose, then the matter is not in my hand at all, for the affair belongs wholly to God, and all decree belongs to God. {But the deaf do not hear the call}; that is, the deaf person does not hear a sound, because his hearing has become corrupt and inoperative, and the condition for hearing along with sound is that there be a receptive locus for it. Likewise, revelation is a cause for the life of hearts and souls and for understanding about God, but when the heart is not receptive to hearing guidance, it stands in relation to guidance and faith as the deaf stands in relation to sounds. Thus these polytheists are deaf to guidance, so their failure to be guided is not strange, especially in this state in which the punishment has not yet come to them nor touched them with its pain.

{46} So if {a breath of the punishment of your Lord} touched them, that is, even a small portion, however slight, of His punishment, {they would surely say: "Woe to us! Indeed we were wrongdoers."} That is, their saying would be nothing but calling for woe and destruction, expressing regret, and acknowledging their wrongdoing, their disbelief, and their deserving of punishment.

{45} That is, {Say}: O Muhammad, to all of mankind: {I only warn you by revelation}; that is, I am only a messenger. I do not bring you anything of my own, nor do I have the treasures of God, nor do I know the unseen, nor do I say that I am an angel. I only warn you with what God has revealed to me. Indeed we were wrongdoers."} That is, their saying would be nothing but calling for woe and destruction, expressing regret, and acknowledging their wrongdoing, their disbelief, and their deserving of punishment.

{47} He, exalted is He, informs of His just judgment and equitable decree among His servants when He gathers them on the Day of Resurrection, and that He will set up for them the just scales, in which will be made manifest the weights of the dharra (speck of dust) by which good deeds and evil deeds are weighed. {So no soul will be wronged}: neither a Muslim nor a disbeliever {in anything}: by having its good deeds diminished or its evil deeds increased. {Even if it is the weight of a mustard seed}, which is the smallest and most insignificant of things, of good or evil, We will bring it and produce it, so that its doer may be recompensed for it. Like His saying: {So whoever does an atom's weight of good will see it. And whoever does an atom's weight of evil will see it} [Qur'an 99:7-8], and {They will say, "Woe to us! What is this book that leaves nothing small or great but has enumerated it?" And they will find what they did present} [Qur'an 18:49]. {And sufficient are We as already reckoners}; meaning by this His noble Self. So He is sufficient as a reckoner: that is, knowing the deeds of His servants, preserving them, recording them in the Book, knowing their measures and the measures of their reward and punishment and what they deserve, and delivering to the workers their recompense.

{48} Often the Exalted combines these two glorious books, which no nation of the world has ever surpassed in excellence, greatness of mention, blessing, or in the guidance and clarity they contain: the Torah and the Qur'an. He informs that He gave Musa (Moses) the Furqan (the Criterion) as a principal gift, and Harun (Aaron) as a follower. The Furqan is the Torah, which distinguishes truth from falsehood and guidance from misguidance. It is {a light}, i.e., a light by which the guided are guided and by which the travellers follow, by which the rulings are known, by which the lawful is distinguished from the unlawful, and which gives light in the darkness of ignorance, innovation and error. It is also ﴿a reminder for the God-conscious﴾, who remember through it what benefits them and what harms them, and through it remember good and evil. He singled out the God-conscious for mention, because they are the ones who benefit from it in knowledge and in action.

{49} Then He explained who the God-conscious are, saying: ﴿those who fear their Lord unseen﴾, i.e., they fear Him in their private state, when people do not see them. If they fear Him when seen, it is all the more so. Thus they refrain from what He has forbidden and perform what He has obligated. ﴿And they are apprehensive of the Hour﴾, i.e., they are fearful and anxious, because of the perfection of their knowledge of their Lord. Thus they combine goodness with fear. The conjunction here is of the type of coordinating distinct attributes that apply to one thing and one described subject.

{50} ﴿And this﴾, i.e., the Qur'an, ﴿is a blessed reminder which We have sent down﴾. He described it with two glorious attributes: that it is a reminder by which every matter is remembered, from knowledge of Allah through His names, attributes and actions, to the qualities and circumstances of the messengers and the friends of Allah, to the rulings of the Shari'ah concerning acts of worship, transactions and other matters, and to the rulings concerning recompense, Paradise and Hell. Thus through it one remembers both the rational and the transmitted matters and proofs. He named it a reminder because it reminds of what Allah has placed in the minds and natural dispositions: belief in true reports, commanding what is rationally good, and forbidding what is rationally evil.

Its being blessed implies the abundance of its good, its growth and its increase. There is nothing greater in blessing than this Qur'an, for every good, favour and increase, whether religious, worldly or in the Hereafter, comes through it and is a result of acting upon it. When it is a blessed reminder, it is obligatory to receive it with acceptance, submission and surrender, to thank Allah for this great gift, to uphold it, and to draw out its blessing by learning its words and meanings.

Its opposite is to face it with the reverse of this condition: turning away from it, dismissing it wholly, denying it, and not believing in it. This is among the greatest disbelief and the most severe ignorance and wrongdoing. For this reason the Exalted rebuked those who denied it, saying: ﴿Will you then deny it?﴾

{51} When Allah mentioned Musa and Muhammad (ﷺ) and their two books, He said: ﴿And We gave Ibrahim his guidance before, and We knew him well.﴾ That is, before the sending of Musa and Muhammad and the revelation of their two books. Allah showed him the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and gave him the right guidance, with which he perfected himself and called people to it, a guidance that He gave to no one among the worlds except Muhammad. He attributed the guidance to Ibrahim because it was guidance proportionate to his state and his high rank. Otherwise, every believer has guidance in proportion to the faith he has. ﴿And We knew him well﴾: that is, We gave him his guidance, singled him out for prophethood and friendship (khullah), and chose him in this world and the next, because We knew that he was worthy of that and suited to it, for his purity and his intelligence.

For this reason He mentioned his argument with his people, his forbidding them from associating partners with Allah, his breaking of the idols, and his holding them to the proof. He said:

{52} ﴿When he said to his father and his people, "What are these images to which you are devoted?"﴾: the images that you have made and carved with your own hands in the likeness of some created beings, ﴿to which you are devoted﴾: that is, remaining upon their worship and constant in it. So what are they? What virtue has been established for them? Where are your minds, which have gone, so that you have spent your times in worshipping them, when you have shaped them and carved them with your own hands? This is one of the greatest wonders: you worship what you carve?!

{53} They answered without any proof, with the answer of one who is powerless and has not the slightest justification in hand. They said: ﴿"We found our fathers doing so."﴾ So we followed their way and imitated them in worshipping them! It is known that the action of any creature other than the messengers is not a proof, and imitating it is not permissible, especially in the foundation of religion and the monotheism of the Lord of the worlds.

{54} For this reason Ibrahim said to them, misguiding them all: ﴿"You and your fathers have certainly been in clear error."﴾ That is, manifest and evident error. {73} Among their righteousness is that He made them leaders who guide by His command. This is among the greatest blessings of Allah upon His servant: that he should be a leader by whom the guided are guided and behind whom the travelers walk. This includes all good, the rights of Allah and the rights of the servants. ﴿And the establishment of prayer and the giving of zakah﴾: this is the mention of the specific after the general, because of the nobility and excellence of these two acts of worship, and because whoever perfects them as commanded is upright in his religion, and whoever neglects them is even more negligent of everything else. So they deserved that worship should be their attribute, and they were characterized by what Allah commanded His creatures, and for which He created them.

{51} When Allah mentioned Musa and Muhammad (ﷺ) and their two books, He said: ﴿And We gave Ibrahim his guidance before, and We knew him well.﴾ That is, before the sending of Musa and Muhammad and the revelation of their two books. Allah showed him the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and gave him the right guidance, with which he perfected himself and called people to it, a guidance that He gave to no one among the worlds except Muhammad. He attributed the guidance to Ibrahim because it was guidance proportionate to his state and his high rank. Otherwise, every believer has guidance in proportion to the faith he has. ﴿And We knew him well﴾: that is, We gave him his guidance, singled him out for prophethood and friendship (khullah), and chose him in this world and the next, because We knew that he was worthy of that and suited to it, for his purity and his intelligence.

For this reason He mentioned his argument with his people, his forbidding them from associating partners with Allah, his breaking of the idols, and his holding them to the proof. He said:

{52} ﴿When he said to his father and his people, "What are these images to which you are devoted?"﴾: the images that you have made and carved with your own hands in the likeness of some created beings, ﴿to which you are devoted﴾: that is, remaining upon their worship and constant in it. So what are they? What virtue has been established for them? Where are your minds, which have gone, so that you have spent your times in worshipping them, when you have shaped them and carved them with your own hands? This is one of the greatest wonders: you worship what you carve?!

{53} They answered without any proof, with the answer of one who is powerless and has not the slightest justification in hand. They said: ﴿"We found our fathers doing so."﴾ So we followed their way and imitated them in worshipping them! It is known that the action of any creature other than the messengers is not a proof, and imitating it is not permissible, especially in the foundation of religion and the monotheism of the Lord of the worlds.

{54} For this reason Ibrahim said to them, misguiding them all: ﴿"You and your fathers have certainly been in clear error."﴾ That is, manifest and evident error. And what error is more extreme than their error in associating partners and abandoning monotheism? That is: what you have said is not fit to be held to. You and they have shared in an error that is clear and obvious to everyone.

{55} ﴿They said﴾, in astonishment at his words and in questioning what he said, and how he began by declaring them foolish and their fathers foolish: ﴿"Have you come to us with the truth, or are you among the jokers?"﴾ That is: is this statement that you have made, and that you have brought to us, true and established, or is your speech to us the speech of a jester who mocks and does not know what he is saying? This is what they intended. They repeated the speech between the two matters because they treated it as settled and known to everyone: that the speech which Ibrahim brought was the speech of a fool who does not understand what he says.

{56} Ibrahim answered them with a reply that showed the reason for their foolishness and the poverty of their minds. He said: ﴿"Rather, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, who created them, and I am a witness to that."﴾ He combined for them the rational proof and the transmitted proof. As for the rational proof: every person knows, even those with whom Ibrahim argued, that Allah alone is the Creator of all creatures, of the children of Adam, the angels, the jinn, the beasts, the heavens and the earth, and the One who manages them in every kind of management. So every creature is originated, managed, and subject to His disposal. This includes everything that is worshipped besides Allah. Is it fitting, for anyone who has even a little sense and discernment, to worship a creature that is subject to disposal, which possesses no benefit, no harm, no death, no life, and no resurrection, and to leave the worship of the Creator, the Provider, the Manager?

As for the transmitted proof: it is what has been related from the messengers, may prayers and peace be upon them. What they brought is protected from error, does not go astray, and does not report anything other than the truth. Among the kinds of this category is the testimony of one of the messengers to that. For this reason Ibrahim said: ﴿"And I am a witness to that"﴾: that Allah alone is the one worshipped, and that the worship of anything other than Him is false. ﴿"Among the witnesses"﴾: and what testimony is higher after the testimony of Allah than the testimony of the messengers, especially those of firm resolve among them, and especially the Friend of the Most Merciful?

{57} When he had shown that their idols had no share in management at all, he wished to show them in fact their powerlessness and their inability to defend themselves, and to plot a plot by which they would be brought to acknowledge that. So he said: ﴿"By Allah, I will surely plot against your idols"﴾: that is, I will break them by way of plotting, ﴿"after you have turned away, retreating."﴾ That is, turning away from them, toward one of their festivals.

{58} When they had turned away, retreating, he went to them secretly, ﴿and he reduced them to fragments﴾: that is, to pieces and shards. They had been gathered in one house, and he broke all of them, ﴿except a big one among them﴾: that is, except their large idol, for he left it for a purpose he would make clear. Consider this remarkable caution. Every object that is abhorred by Allah is not called by terms of exaltation except in the sense of its being attributed to its adherents. {59} When they saw what had befallen their idols of humiliation and disgrace, ﴿they said, "Who has done this to our gods? The true wrongdoer is the one who takes them as gods, and who has seen what was done to them.

{60} ﴿They said, "We heard a youth mention them"﴾: that is, speak ill of them and blame them. Whoever is of such a character must be the one who broke them, or else one of them heard him saying that he would plot against them. ﴿"He is called Ibrahim."﴾

{61} When they were certain that it was Ibrahim, ﴿they said, "Then bring him before the eyes of the people"﴾: that is, before their sight and hearing, ﴿"that they may bear witness."﴾ That is, they may attend and see what will be done to the one who broke their gods. This was what Ibrahim intended and aimed at: that the clarification of the truth should take place in the presence of the people, so that they might witness the truth and the proof might be established against them. This is like what Musa said when he made an appointment with Pharaoh: ﴿"Your appointment is the day of adornment, and let the people be gathered in the forenoon."﴾

{62} When the people had gathered and Ibrahim was brought, they said to him: ﴿"Have you done this to our gods, O Ibrahim?"﴾ This is a question of confirmation: that is, what has emboldened you? What has led you to undertake this matter?

{63} Ibrahim said, while the people were watching: ﴿"Rather, this one among them, the big one, did it."﴾ That is, he broke them in anger at them, since they were worshipped alongside him, and he wanted worship to be directed from you to your great idol alone. If they have speech, they will answer you in this regard. But I, and you, and everyone knows that they do not speak, do not talk, and neither benefit nor harm, nor even defend themselves against one who wants to harm them.

{64} ﴿So they returned to themselves﴾: that is, their minds became settled upon them, and their wits came back to them. {65} But they did not remain in this state; rather, ﴿they were overturned upon their heads﴾: that is, the matter turned against them, their minds were reversed, and their wits went astray. {51} When Allah mentioned Musa and Muhammad (ﷺ) and their two books, He said: ﴿And We gave Ibrahim his guidance before, and We knew him well.﴾ That is, before the sending of Musa and Muhammad and the revelation of their two books. He attributed the guidance to Ibrahim because it was guidance proportionate to his state and his high rank. Otherwise, every believer has guidance in proportion to the faith he has. ﴿And We knew him well﴾: that is, We gave him his guidance, singled him out for prophethood and friendship (khullah), and chose him in this world and the next, because We knew that he was worthy of that and suited to it, for his purity and his intelligence.

For this reason He mentioned his argument with his people, his forbidding them from associating partners with Allah, his breaking of the idols, and his holding them to the proof. He said:

{52} ﴿When he said to his father and his people, "What are these images to which you are devoted?"﴾: the images that you have made and carved with your own hands in the likeness of some created beings, ﴿to which you are devoted﴾: that is, remaining upon their worship and constant in it. Where are your minds, which have gone, so that you have spent your times in worshipping them, when you have shaped them and carved them with your own hands? This is one of the greatest wonders: you worship what you carve?!

{53} They answered without any proof, with the answer of one who is powerless and has not the slightest justification in hand. They said: ﴿"We found our fathers doing so."﴾ So we followed their way and imitated them in worshipping them! It is known that the action of any creature other than the messengers is not a proof, and imitating it is not permissible, especially in the foundation of religion and the monotheism of the Lord of the worlds.

{54} For this reason Ibrahim said to them, misguiding them all: ﴿"You and your fathers have certainly been in clear error."﴾ That is, manifest and evident error. And what error is more extreme than their error in associating partners and abandoning monotheism? That is: what you have said is not fit to be held to. You and they have shared in an error that is clear and obvious to everyone.

{55} ﴿They said﴾, in astonishment at his words and in questioning what he said, and how he began by declaring them foolish and their fathers foolish: ﴿"Have you come to us with the truth, or are you among the jokers?"﴾ That is: is this statement that you have made, and that you have brought to us, true and established, or is your speech to us the speech of a jester who mocks and does not know what he is saying? This is what they intended. They repeated the speech between the two matters because they treated it as settled and known to everyone: that the speech which Ibrahim brought was the speech of a fool who does not understand what he says.

{56} Ibrahim answered them with a reply that showed the reason for their foolishness and the poverty of their minds. He said: ﴿"Rather, your Lord is the Lord of the heavens and the earth, who created them, and I am a witness to that."﴾ He combined for them the rational proof and the transmitted proof. As for the rational proof: every person knows, even those with whom Ibrahim argued, that Allah alone is the Creator of all creatures, of the children of Adam, the angels, the jinn, the beasts, the heavens and the earth, and the One who manages them in every kind of management. So every creature is originated, managed, and subject to His disposal. This includes everything that is worshipped besides Allah. Is it fitting, for anyone who has even a little sense and discernment, to worship a creature that is subject to disposal, which possesses no benefit, no harm, no death, no life, and no resurrection, and to leave the worship of the Creator, the Provider, the Manager?

As for the transmitted proof: it is what has been related from the messengers, may prayers and peace be upon them. What they brought is protected from error, does not go astray, and does not report anything other than the truth. Among the kinds of this category is the testimony of one of the messengers to that. For this reason Ibrahim said: ﴿"And I am a witness to that"﴾: that Allah alone is the one worshipped, and that the worship of anything other than Him is false. ﴿"Among the witnesses"﴾: and what testimony is higher after the testimony of Allah than the testimony of the messengers, especially those of firm resolve among them, and especially the Friend of the Most Merciful?

{58} When they had turned away, retreating, he went to them secretly, ﴿and he reduced them to fragments﴾: that is, to pieces and shards. {60} ﴿They said, "We heard a youth mention them"﴾: that is, speak ill of them and blame them. Whoever is of such a character must be the one who broke them, or else one of them heard him saying that he would plot against them. ﴿"He is called Ibrahim."﴾

{61} When they were certain that it was Ibrahim, ﴿they said, "Then bring him before the eyes of the people"﴾: that is, before their sight and hearing, ﴿"that they may bear witness."﴾ That is, they may attend and see what will be done to the one who broke their gods. This is like what Musa said when he made an appointment with Pharaoh: ﴿"Your appointment is the day of adornment, and let the people be gathered in the forenoon."﴾

{58} When they had turned away, retreating, he went to them secretly, ﴿and he reduced them to fragments﴾: that is, to pieces and shards. They had been gathered in one house, and he broke all of them, ﴿except a big one among them﴾: that is, except their large idol, for he left it for a purpose he would make clear. Consider this remarkable caution. Every object that is abhorred by Allah is not called by terms of exaltation except in the sense of its being attributed to its adherents. Thus, when the Prophet (ﷺ) wrote to the polytheist kings of the earth, he would say: "To the great one of Persia..." "To the great one of Rome..." and the like, and he never said "To the Great One." Here Allah said: ﴿except a big one among them﴾, and He did not say "a big one from among their idols." So this must be noticed, and one must be cautious not to exalt what Allah has debased, except when it is attributed to the one who exalts it. As for His words ﴿"that they might return to it"﴾: that is, Ibrahim left this idol of theirs unbroken so that they would return to him, would hear his argument, would turn to it, and would not turn away from it. For this reason, at its end, it says: ﴿"So they turned back to themselves."﴾

{59} When they saw what had befallen their idols of humiliation and disgrace, ﴿they said, "Who has done this to our gods? Indeed, he is of the wrongdoers."﴾ So they accused Ibrahim of the wrongdoing that they themselves deserved, since they were the ones who worshipped them, while he broke them. They did not realize that his breaking them was among his finest virtues, and part of his justice and his monotheism. The true wrongdoer is the one who takes them as gods, and who has seen what was done to them.

{60} ﴿They said, "We heard a youth mention them"﴾: that is, speak ill of them and blame them. Whoever is of such a character must be the one who broke them, or else one of them heard him saying that he would plot against them. ﴿"He is called Ibrahim."﴾

{61} When they were certain that it was Ibrahim, ﴿they said, "Then bring him before the eyes of the people"﴾: that is, before their sight and hearing, ﴿"that they may bear witness."﴾ That is, they may attend and see what will be done to the one who broke their gods. This was what Ibrahim intended and aimed at: that the clarification of the truth should take place in the presence of the people, so that they might witness the truth and the proof might be established against them. This is like what Musa said when he made an appointment with Pharaoh: ﴿"Your appointment is the day of adornment, and let the people be gathered in the forenoon."﴾

{62} When the people had gathered and Ibrahim was brought, they said to him: ﴿"Have you done this to our gods, O Ibrahim?"﴾ This is a question of confirmation: that is, what has emboldened you? What has led you to undertake this matter?

{63} Ibrahim said, while the people were watching: ﴿"Rather, this one among them, the big one, did it."﴾ That is, he broke them in anger at them, since they were worshipped alongside him, and he wanted worship to be directed from you to your great idol alone. This statement from Ibrahim was intended to silence the opponent and establish the proof against him. For this reason he said: ﴿"So ask them, if they can speak."﴾ He meant the broken idols: ask them why they were broken? And as for the idol that was not broken: ask it why it broke the others? If they have speech, they will answer you in this regard. But I, and you, and everyone knows that they do not speak, do not talk, and neither benefit nor harm, nor even defend themselves against one who wants to harm them.

{64} ﴿So they returned to themselves﴾: that is, their minds became settled upon them, and their wits came back to them. They knew that they were astray in worshipping them, and they acknowledged against themselves wrongdoing and polytheism. ﴿They said, "Indeed, you are the wrongdoers."﴾ Thus the goal was achieved, and the proof was binding upon them through their acknowledgment that what they held was false, and that their action was disbelief and wrongdoing.

{65} But they did not remain in this state; rather, ﴿they were overturned upon their heads﴾: that is, the matter turned against them, their minds were reversed, and their wits went astray. They said to Ibrahim: ﴿"You certainly know that these do not speak."﴾ So how do you mock us and ridicule us, and command us to ask them, when you know that they do not speak?

{66} Ibrahim said, rebuking them and declaring their polytheism before the assembled multitude, and showing that their gods do not deserve worship: ﴿"Do you worship, besides Allah, that which can neither benefit you at all nor harm you?"﴾ That is, no benefit and no removal of harm.

{67} ﴿"Uff to you, and to what you worship besides Allah!"﴾ That is: how misguided you are, how losing your bargain is, and how base you are, you and what you worship besides Allah! If you had understanding, you would recognize this condition. But when you lost reason and committed ignorance and error with open eyes, the beasts became better in state than you.

{68} Then, when he had silenced them and they could produce no proof, they resorted to their strength to punish him. ﴿They said, "Burn him and support your gods, if you are going to act."﴾ That is: kill him in the most horrible of deaths, by burning, out of anger for your gods and in support of them. Woe to them, utter woe, for worshipping one whom they themselves acknowledged needs their help, and taking him as a god!

{69} Allah gave victory to His Friend when they cast him into the fire, and He said to it: ﴿"O fire, be coolness and safety upon Ibrahim!"﴾ So it became cool and safe for him. No harm touched him in it, and he felt no hardship.

{70} ﴿And they intended a plot against him﴾: when they resolved to burn him, ﴿but We made them the greatest losers﴾: that is, in this world and the Hereafter, just as Allah made His Friend and his followers the winners and the successful.

{71} ﴿And We delivered him and Lut﴾: this is because none of his people believed in him except Lut, peace be upon him. It was said that he was his nephew. Allah delivered him and he migrated ﴿to the land which We have blessed for the worlds﴾: that is, the Levant. He departed from his people in Babylon in the land of Iraq. ﴿And he said, "Indeed, I am migrating to my Lord; indeed, He is the Mighty, the Wise."﴾ Among the blessings of the Levant is that many prophets lived in it, and that Allah chose it as the place of migration for His Friend. In it is one of His three sacred houses, which is the Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem).

{72} ﴿And We gave him﴾: when he withdrew from his people, ﴿Ishaq and Yaqub﴾, the son of Ishaq, ﴿as an additional gift﴾: after he had grown old and his wife was barren, so the angels gave him the good news of Ishaq. ﴿And after Ishaq, Yaqub﴾. Yaqub is Israel, from whom came the great nation, and Isma'il son of Ibrahim, from whom came the noble Arab nation, and from his descendants came the master of the first and the last. ﴿And all of them﴾: Ibrahim, Ishaq and Yaqub, ﴿We made righteous﴾: that is, upholding the rights of Allah and the rights of His servants.

{73} Among their righteousness is that He made them leaders who guide by His command. This is among the greatest blessings of Allah upon His servant: that he should be a leader by whom the guided are guided and behind whom the travelers walk. That was because they were patient, and because they were certain of the signs of Allah. His words ﴿"guiding by Our command"﴾: that is, guiding people to Our religion, not commanding by the desires of their own souls, but by the command of Allah and His religion, and following His good pleasure. A servant does not become a leader until he calls to the command of Allah. ﴿And We revealed to them the doing of good deeds﴾: they do them and call people to them. This includes all good, the rights of Allah and the rights of the servants. ﴿And the establishment of prayer and the giving of zakah﴾: this is the mention of the specific after the general, because of the nobility and excellence of these two acts of worship, and because whoever perfects them as commanded is upright in his religion, and whoever neglects them is even more negligent of everything else. Prayer is the most excellent of the deeds in which is His right, and zakah is the most excellent of the deeds in which is kindness to His creatures. ﴿And they were worshippers of Us﴾: that is, not of anyone else, ﴿devoted to worship﴾: that is, constant in heartfelt, spoken and bodily acts of worship during most of their times. So they deserved that worship should be their attribute, and they were characterized by what Allah commanded His creatures, and for which He created them.

{74} This is praise from Allah for His messenger Lut, upon him be peace, for his knowledge of the sacred law (*shar'i*) and his judging between people with what is correct and sound. Allah sent him to his people, calling them to worship Allah and forbidding them from the abominations they were engaged in. He remained calling them, but they did not respond to him. So Allah overturned their dwellings upon them and punished them all, every one, because they ﴿were a people of evil, defiantly disobedient﴾. They denied the caller and threatened him with expulsion. Allah saved Lut and his family, and commanded him to travel with them by night so that they would be far from the town. So they traveled and were delivered, by the favor and kindness of Allah toward them.

{75} ﴿And We admitted him into Our mercy﴾: whoever enters it is among the secure from every fear, attaining every good, happiness, righteousness, joy, and praise. This is because he was among the righteous, whose deeds were sound and whose states were pure, and Allah set right whatever in them was corrupt. Righteousness is the cause of a servant's entry into the mercy of Allah, just as corruption is the cause of his being deprived of mercy and good. The greatest of people in righteousness are the prophets, upon them be peace, and for this reason Allah describes them with righteousness. Sulayman, upon him be peace, said: ﴿And admit me, by Your mercy, among Your righteous servants﴾.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 21, verses 76–77:

{76–77} That is: remember Our servant and messenger Noah (peace be upon him), who was often praised and extolled when Allah sent him to his people. He remained among them for nine hundred and fifty years, calling them to worship Allah and forbidding them from associating partners with Him. He repeated and reiterated the message among them, calling them secretly and openly, by night and by day. When he saw that admonition was not effective with them and that reproof did not benefit them, he called upon his Lord and said: ﴿My Lord, do not leave upon the earth any of the disbelievers as a dwelling. Indeed, if You leave them, they will mislead Your servants and will not beget except immoral and ungrateful disbelievers.﴾ So Allah answered his supplication, drowned them, and did not leave any of them behind. Allah saved Noah, his family, and those who were with him of the believers in the laden ship, and He made his offspring the ones who remained, and Allah granted him victory over his mocking people.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 21, verse 78–82:

{78} That is: mention these two noble prophets, Dawud and Sulayman, praising and honoring them; for Allah gave them wide knowledge and judgment among the servants. The evidence is His saying: ﴿When they both judged concerning the field, when the sheep of the people pastured in it by night, and We were witnesses to their judgment.﴾ That is: when the owner of a field came to them to judge between him and the owners of the sheep, whose flock had strayed into his field, grazing by night, eating what was in his trees and grazing his crops. Dawud, peace be upon him, judged that the sheep should belong to the owner of the field, in view of the negligence of their owners, and so punished them with this penalty. Sulayman judged in this matter with a judgment that agreed with what is right: that the owners of the sheep hand over their sheep to the owner of the field, so that he benefits from their milk and wool, while they tend the orchard of the owner of the field until it returns to its former state. When it has returned to its state, the two of them return, and each takes back his property. This was part of the completeness of his understanding and shrewdness, peace be upon him.

{79} Therefore He said: ﴿And We gave understanding of it to Sulayman﴾; that is, We made him understand this case. This does not indicate that Dawud was not given understanding of other matters, and for this reason it was singled out for mention. The evidence is His saying: ﴿And to each We gave judgment and knowledge﴾: to both Dawud and Sulayman We gave judgment and knowledge. This is evidence that a judge may hit the truth and the right, and may also err; and he is not blameworthy if he errs while exerting his utmost effort (ijtihad).
Then He mentioned what was specific to each of them, saying: ﴿And We subjected the mountains to glorify [Allah] along with Dawud, and the birds [as well]﴾. This was because he was among the people most devoted to worship and most abundant in the remembrance, glorification and exaltation of Allah. Allah had given him a beautiful voice, of such sweetness, softness and resonance as He had given to no other creature. So when he glorified and praised Allah, the solid mountains and the mute birds responded to him. This was Allah's favor and kindness toward him, and for this reason He said: ﴿And We were ever doing [that].﴾

{80} ﴿And We taught him the making of coats of armor for you﴾; that is, Allah taught Dawud, peace be upon him, the craft of making armor. He was the first to make and teach it, and his craft spread to those after him. Allah softened the iron for him and taught him how to weave it. Its benefit is great: ﴿to protect you from your violence﴾; that is, it is a shield and protection for you during war and the intensity of battle. ﴿Then will you be grateful?﴾ for the favor of Allah upon you, in that He brought it about through the hand of His servant Dawud? As Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And He made for you garments to protect you from the heat, and garments to protect you from your violence. Thus does He complete His favor upon you that you might submit.﴾
It is possible that Allah's teaching Dawud the craft of armor and softening it was a matter beyond the ordinary course of things, and that it was as the exegetes said: Allah softened the iron for him, so that he worked it like dough and clay without melting it over fire.
It is also possible that Allah's teaching him was in accordance with the customary course, and that the softening of the iron for him was by means of the causes known today for melting it, and this is the apparent meaning. For Allah bestowed a favor [by this] upon the servants and commanded them to be grateful for it; and had his craft not been among the matters that Allah made within the capacity of the servants, He would not have bestowed this favor upon them and mentioned its benefit. For the armor that Dawud, peace be upon him, made cannot be meant as specific pieces, rather the favor is in the kind. The interpretation mentioned by the exegetes has no evidence except His saying: ﴿And We softened for him the iron﴾, and there is nothing in it indicating that the softening was without cause. And Allah knows best.

{81} ﴿And to Sulayman [We subjected] the wind﴾; that is, We subjected it, ﴿blowing forcefully﴾; that is, swift in its passage, ﴿running by his command﴾: wherever he directed it, it complied with his command. Its morning course was a month and its evening course a month, ﴿to the land which We had blessed﴾: this is the land of the Levant (al-Sham), where his residence was. So it would travel by the wind eastward and westward, and its shelter and return would be to the blessed land. ﴿And We were, of all things, Knowing﴾: Our knowledge encompasses all things, and We knew of Dawud and Sulayman what brought them to what We have mentioned.

{82} ﴿And of the devils were those who dove for him and did work other than that﴾: this too is among the distinctive features of Sulayman, peace be upon him: Allah subjected to him the devils and the ifrits, and empowered him to make them work at tasks that most others could not perform. Among them were those who dove for him into the sea and brought out pearls, coral and other things, and among them were those who made for him ﴿arches, statues, bowls like reservoirs, and fixed cooking pots﴾. He subjected a group of them to build the Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem's sanctuary), and they remained at their work after his death for a year until they knew of his death, as will come, Allah willing. ﴿And We were, for them, Guardians﴾; that is, they were unable to refuse or disobey him, rather Allah preserved them for him by His strength, might and authority.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 21, verse 78–82:

{78} That is: mention these two noble prophets, Dawud and Sulayman, praising and honoring them; for Allah gave them wide knowledge and judgment among the servants. The evidence is His saying: ﴿When they both judged concerning the field, when the sheep of the people pastured in it by night, and We were witnesses to their judgment.﴾ That is: when the owner of a field came to them to judge between him and the owners of the sheep, whose flock had strayed into his field, grazing by night, eating what was in his trees and grazing his crops. Dawud, peace be upon him, judged that the sheep should belong to the owner of the field, in view of the negligence of their owners, and so punished them with this penalty. Sulayman judged in this matter with a judgment that agreed with what is right: that the owners of the sheep hand over their sheep to the owner of the field, so that he benefits from their milk and wool, while they tend the orchard of the owner of the field until it returns to its former state. When it has returned to its state, the two of them return, and each takes back his property. This was part of the completeness of his understanding and shrewdness, peace be upon him.

{79} Therefore He said: ﴿And We gave understanding of it to Sulayman﴾; that is, We made him understand this case. This does not indicate that Dawud was not given understanding of other matters, and for this reason it was singled out for mention. The evidence is His saying: ﴿And to each We gave judgment and knowledge﴾: to both Dawud and Sulayman We gave judgment and knowledge. This is evidence that a judge may hit the truth and the right, and may also err; and he is not blameworthy if he errs while exerting his utmost effort (ijtihad).
Then He mentioned what was specific to each of them, saying: ﴿And We subjected the mountains to glorify [Allah] along with Dawud, and the birds [as well]﴾. This was because he was among the people most devoted to worship and most abundant in the remembrance, glorification and exaltation of Allah. Allah had given him a beautiful voice, of such sweetness, softness and resonance as He had given to no other creature. So when he glorified and praised Allah, the solid mountains and the mute birds responded to him. This was Allah's favor and kindness toward him, and for this reason He said: ﴿And We were ever doing [that].﴾

{80} ﴿And We taught him the making of coats of armor for you﴾; that is, Allah taught Dawud, peace be upon him, the craft of making armor. He was the first to make and teach it, and his craft spread to those after him. Allah softened the iron for him and taught him how to weave it. Its benefit is great: ﴿to protect you from your violence﴾; that is, it is a shield and protection for you during war and the intensity of battle. ﴿Then will you be grateful?﴾ for the favor of Allah upon you, in that He brought it about through the hand of His servant Dawud? As Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And He made for you garments to protect you from the heat, and garments to protect you from your violence. Thus does He complete His favor upon you that you might submit.﴾
It is possible that Allah's teaching Dawud the craft of armor and softening it was a matter beyond the ordinary course of things, and that it was as the exegetes said: Allah softened the iron for him, so that he worked it like dough and clay without melting it over fire.
It is also possible that Allah's teaching him was in accordance with the customary course, and that the softening of the iron for him was by means of the causes known today for melting it, and this is the apparent meaning. For the armor that Dawud, peace be upon him, made cannot be meant as specific pieces, rather the favor is in the kind. The interpretation mentioned by the exegetes has no evidence except His saying: ﴿And We softened for him the iron﴾, and there is nothing in it indicating that the softening was without cause. And Allah knows best.

{81} ﴿And to Sulayman [We subjected] the wind﴾; that is, We subjected it, ﴿blowing forcefully﴾; that is, swift in its passage, ﴿running by his command﴾: wherever he directed it, it complied with his command. Its morning course was a month and its evening course a month, ﴿to the land which We had blessed﴾: this is the land of the Levant (al-Sham), where his residence was. So it would travel by the wind eastward and westward, and its shelter and return would be to the blessed land. ﴿And We were, of all things, Knowing﴾: Our knowledge encompasses all things, and We knew of Dawud and Sulayman what brought them to what We have mentioned.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 21, verses 85–86:

{85} That is: Remember Our servants who were chosen and Our prophets who were sent, and praise them with the most eloquent praise: {Isma'il} the son of Ibrahim, {and Idris and Dhu'l-Kifl}: two prophets from among the prophets of the Children of Israel. {All} of those mentioned {were among the patient}. Patience (sabr) is restraining the self and preventing it from what it naturally inclines toward. This encompasses the three types of patience: patience in obedience to Allah, patience in refraining from disobedience to Allah, and patience in the painful decrees of Allah.

A servant does not deserve the name of complete patience until he gives each of these three its due. These prophets, peace be upon them, were described by Allah as patient, which indicates that they fulfilled these three in full and carried them out as they should be carried out.

{86} He also described them as righteous (salah), which includes: the righteousness of the heart through knowing Allah, loving Him, and turning to Him at all times; the righteousness of the tongue, by its being moist with the remembrance of Allah; and the righteousness of the limbs by their occupation with obedience to Allah and their restraint from sins.
By their patience and their righteousness, Allah admitted them by His mercy, placed them with their brethren among the messengers, and rewarded them with both the swift reward and the deferred reward. Even if their reward had consisted only of Allah, may He be exalted, making mention of them among the worlds and granting them a tongue of truthfulness among the later generations, it would have been sufficient as a token of honor and excellence.
