Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 21, verses 87–88:

{87–88} That is: Remember Our servant and messenger {Dha al-Nun} (the Man of the Whale), who is Yunus (Jonah); that is, the companion of the Nun (the fish), with fair mention and good praise. Allah the Exalted sent him to his people, and he called them, but they did not believe. So he promised them the descent of punishment at a term he set for them, and the punishment came to them, and they saw it plainly. Then they cried out to Allah, wailed, and repented, so Allah removed the punishment from them, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Why was there not a town that believed so that its faith benefited it, except the people of Yunus? When they believed, We removed from them the punishment of disgrace in the life of this world and let them enjoy for a time.﴾ And He said: ﴿And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more. And they believed, so We let them enjoy for a time.﴾ This great nation who believed through the call of Yunus is among his greatest virtues. But he, peace be upon him, went off in anger and fled from his Lord because of a sin among the sins which Allah did not mention to us in His Book, and there is no need for us to specify it; due to His saying: ﴿When he fled to the laden ship... while he was blameworthy﴾; that is, one who did what he could be blamed for. [It appears that his haste, his anger at his people, and his departure from among them before Allah commanded him to do so.] He thought that Allah would not have power over him; that is, that He would not constrict him in the belly of the fish, or he thought that he would escape Allah the Exalted. There is no objection to such a thought arising in the perfect among creation, in a manner that does not settle or persist. So he boarded a ship with some people, and they cast lots as to which of them they would throw into the sea, for they feared drowning if they all remained. The lot fell upon Yunus, so the whale swallowed him and went with him into the darkness of the seas. He called out in those darknesses: ﴿There is no god but You; glory be to You; indeed I have been of the wrongdoers.﴾ He affirmed for Allah the Exalted the perfection of divinity, declared Him free of every deficiency, defect, and blemish, and acknowledged the wrong he had done to himself and his offense. Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And had he not been of those who glorify [Allah], he would have remained in its belly until the Day they are resurrected.﴾ For this reason, He said here: ﴿So We answered him and saved him from the distress﴾; that is, the hardship into which he had fallen. ﴿And thus do We save the believers.﴾ This is a promise and good tidings to every believer who falls into hardship and distress: that Allah the Exalted will surely deliver him from it, remove it from him, and ease it for him because of his faith, just as He did with Yunus, peace be upon him.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 21, verse 89–90:

{89} That is: "Remember Our servant and messenger Zakariyya (Zechariah)," mentioning him with honour and spreading his virtues and merits, among which is this great merit, which includes his sincere counsel to the creation and the mercy of God toward him. And that: {he called upon his Lord, "My Lord, do not leave me alone (fard)"}; that is, {he said, "My Lord, indeed my bones have weakened and my head has glistened with grey hair, and I have never been unblessed in my supplication to You, my Lord. And indeed I fear my successors after me, and my wife is barren, so grant me from Yourself an heir, who will inherit me and inherit from the family of Ya'qub, and make him, my Lord, pleasing."} From these verses we learn that his saying, {"My Lord, do not leave me alone"}, was because, as his end drew near, he feared that no one would stand after him in his place in calling to God and giving sincere counsel to the servants of God, and that he would be alone in his time without any who would support him and help him in what he had undertaken. {And You are the best of inheritors}; that is, the best of those who remain, and the best of those who succeed me with goodness. You are more merciful to Your servants than I am, but I desire that which will set my heart at rest, settle my soul, and whose reward will weigh in my scales.

{90} {So We responded to him and granted him Yahya (John)}: the noble Prophet, of whom God had not made any namesake before him, {and We made his wife fit for him}: after she had been barren, her womb not being suitable for childbearing, God made her womb fit for conception for the sake of His prophet Zakariyya. This is among the benefits of the good companion and the righteous associate: that he is blessed for his companion, so Yahya became shared between the two parents. When He mentioned these prophets and messengers each individually, He then praised them collectively, saying: {Indeed they used to hasten to good deeds}; that is, they would hasten toward them, perform them in their virtuous times, complete them in the proper and fitting manner, and they would not leave any virtue they were able to do without seizing the opportunity for it. {And they used to call upon Us with hope and fear}; that is, they would ask Us for the things desired of the benefits of this world and the Hereafter, and seek refuge with Us from the things feared of the harms of both abodes, and they were ones who hoped and feared, not heedless, negligent, or self-deluded. {And they were humble before Us}; that is, submissive, lowly, and supplicating, and this is due to the perfection of their knowledge of their Lord.

{90} {So We responded to him and granted him Yahya (John)}: the noble Prophet, of whom God had not made any namesake before him, {and We made his wife fit for him}: after she had been barren, her womb not being suitable for childbearing, God made her womb fit for conception for the sake of His prophet Zakariyya. This is among the benefits of the good companion and the righteous associate: that he is blessed for his companion, so Yahya became shared between the two parents. When He mentioned these prophets and messengers each individually, He then praised them collectively, saying: {Indeed they used to hasten to good deeds}; that is, they would hasten toward them, perform them in their virtuous times, complete them in the proper and fitting manner, and they would not leave any virtue they were able to do without seizing the opportunity for it. {And they used to call upon Us with hope and fear}; that is, they would ask Us for the things desired of the benefits of this world and the Hereafter, and seek refuge with Us from the things feared of the harms of both abodes, and they were ones who hoped and feared, not heedless, negligent, or self-deluded. {And they were humble before Us}; that is, submissive, lowly, and supplicating, and this is due to the perfection of their knowledge of their Lord.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 21, verses 91–94:

{91} That is: remember Maryam (peace be upon her), praising her, making clear her rank, and displaying her nobility. So He said: ﴿And she who guarded her chastity﴾; that is, she preserved it from what is unlawful and from approaching it, and even from what is lawful, so she did not marry, being occupied with worship and devoting her time entirely to serving her Lord. When Jibril came to her in the form of a man, perfect in creation and beauty, ﴿she said: "Indeed, I seek refuge in the Most Merciful from you, if you are God-fearing."﴾ Allah rewarded her in kind for her deeds and granted her a child without a father; rather, Jibril breathed into her, and she conceived by the permission of Allah. ﴿And We made her and her son a sign for the worlds﴾; in that she conceived him and gave birth to him without the touch of anyone, and in that he spoke in the cradle, and He cleared her of what the accusers suspected of her, and he informed about himself in that state, and Allah brought about through his hands the extraordinary events and miracles that are well known. Thus she and her son were a sign for the worlds, spoken of generation after generation, and those who reflect take lesson from them.

{92} When He had mentioned the prophets (peace be upon them), He addressed the people, saying: ﴿Indeed, this community of yours is one community﴾; that is, these mentioned messengers are your community and your imams, by whom you are guided and by whose guidance you follow. They are all upon one religion and one path, and the Lord is also one. Hence He said: ﴿And I am your Lord﴾, who created you and nurtured you with My blessings in religion and in this world. So when the Lord is one, the Prophet is one, and the religion is one, namely the worship of Allah alone without partner in all kinds of worship, then your duty and obligation is to uphold it. Hence He said: ﴿so worship Me﴾; He made worship follow what preceded it with the fa', the way a effect follows its cause.

{93} It would have been fitting to unite upon this matter and not to divide over it, but transgression and aggression refused except division and fragmentation. Hence He said: ﴿but they cut their affair among themselves into sects﴾; that is, the factions who claim to follow the prophets split into groups and scattered, each claiming that the truth is with it and falsehood is with the other party, ﴿each party rejoicing in what they have﴾. It is known that the one among them who is right is the one who follows the upright religion and the straight path, following the prophets. This will become evident when the veil is lifted, concealment ends, and Allah gathers the people for the judgment; then the truthful will be distinguished from the liar. Hence He said: ﴿all to Us they will return﴾; from the divided sects and others, that is, We will repay them with the most complete recompense.

{94} Then He detailed their recompense, both explicitly and by implication, saying: ﴿So whoever does righteous deeds﴾; that is, the deeds prescribed by the messengers and urged by the books, ﴿while being a believer﴾ in Allah, His messengers, and what they brought, ﴿his effort will not be rejected﴾; that is, We will not waste his striving or nullify it, but rather We will multiply it for him many times over. ﴿And indeed, We are recording it for him﴾; that is, We record it for him in the Preserved Tablet and in the scrolls kept by the recording angels. And whoever does not do righteous deeds, or does them while not being a believer, then he is deprived and a loser in his religion and his worldly life.

Commentary of Ibn Sa'di (Taysir al-Karim al-Rahman) on surah 21, verse 96–97:

{96} This is a warning from Allah to people who persist in disbelief and sins, and that the opening of Ya'juj and Ma'juj (Gog and Magog) is near. They are two great tribes from the children of Adam. Dhul-Qarnayn barred them off when the corruption they caused in the earth was complained of to him, and at the end of time the barrier will be opened for them, and they will come out to the people. In this state, and with the description Allah mentioned, "from every elevated place," which is the hadb, "they will swarm" (yanisiluna); i.e., they will hasten.

In this is an indication of their astonishing numbers and their speed across the earth, either by their own selves or by means of the causes Allah has created for them that bring the distant near to them and make the difficult easy for them. It also indicates that they will subdue people and prevail over them in this world, and that no one will have the power to fight them.

{97} {And the true promise draws near}; i.e., the Day of Resurrection, which Allah promised to bring. His promise is true and sincere. On that day, the eyes of the disbelievers will stare fixedly from the intensity of terror, the alarming horrors, and the dreadful upheavals, and they will recognize their misdeeds and sins. They will call out with woe, destruction, regret, and anguish over what has passed, and they will say: "Indeed we were {in heedlessness of this} great Day, and we never ceased to be absorbed in it and to enjoy the pleasures of the world until certainty came to us and we arrived at the Resurrection." Had anyone been going to die from regret and anguish, they would have died. {Rather, we were wrongdoers}: they acknowledged their wrongdoing and Allah's justice toward them. Then they will be commanded to the Fire, they and what they used to worship. Therefore He said:

{99} The wisdom in the idols entering the Fire, though they are inanimate and do not reason, and bear no sin, is to demonstrate the falsehood of those who took them as deities, and to increase their punishment. Hence He said: {Had these been gods, they would not have entered it}. This is like His saying, exalted is He: {so that He may make clear to them that about which they differ, and that those who disbelieved may know that they were liars} [16:39]. Both the worshippers and the worshipped therein are eternal; they will not leave it, nor will they be moved from it.

{100} {For them therein is a groaning}: from the intensity of the punishment. {And they therein do not hear}: deaf, dumb, and blind; or they hear none of the sounds except its sound, due to the intensity of its boiling, the severity of its roaring, and its rage.

{101-102} The entry of the deities of the polytheists into the Fire refers only to the idols, or to whoever was worshipped while being content with his worship. As for the Messiah, Uzayr, the angels, and others of the friends of God who were worshipped, they will not be punished therein, and they fall under His saying: {Indeed those for whom the best [reward] has preceded from Us}; that is, the preceding good fortune was decreed for them in God's knowledge, in the Preserved Tablet, and in facilitating for them the ease [of the path] in this world toward ease and righteous deeds. {Those will be kept far from it}: from the Fire, {kept far}: so they will not enter it, nor will they be near it; rather they will be removed from it to the utmost distance, so that they will not hear its faint sound, nor see its form. {And they, in what their souls desire, will abide eternally}: of foods, drinks, spouses, and sights, such as no eye has seen, no ear has heard, and it has not occurred to the heart of any human; this continues for them, its goodness increasing over ages.

{103} {The greatest terror will not grieve them}; that is, the greatest terror will not disturb them when people are struck by it, and that is the Day of Resurrection, when the Fire draws near, raging against the disbelievers and the disobedient. People will be terrified by that event, but these will not be grieved by it, because of their knowledge of what they are going to, and because God has granted them security from what they fear. {And the angels will receive them}: when they are raised from their graves, and they come upon swift mounts in delegations for their resurrection, congratulating them and saying: {This is your Day which you were promised}. So let what God has promised you be pleasant for you, let your joy at the honour that lies before you be great, and let your delight and happiness increase at the security God has granted you from fears and hardships.

{104} Almighty God informs us that on the Day of Resurrection He will fold up the heavens, despite their greatness and vastness, just as a scribe folds the scroll (al-sijill), that is, the sheet on which something is written. Their stars will be scattered, their sun and moon will be wound up, and they will be removed from their places. ﴿As We originated the first creation, We will repeat it﴾: that is, Our restoring of creation is like Our originating of it. Just as We originated their creation when they were nothing, so We will restore them after their death. ﴿A promise binding upon Us. Indeed, We are ever doing [it]﴾: We will carry out what We have promised, because of the perfection of His power and because nothing can resist Him.

{105} ﴿And We had already written in the Zabur﴾: the Zabur is the written book (al-kitab al-mazbur), and what is meant is the revealed books, such as the Torah and the like. ﴿after the reminder﴾: that is, We wrote it in the revealed books after having written it in the earlier book, which is the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh al-mahfuz) and the Mother of the Book (umm al-kitab), with which all the subsequent decrees agree. What was written therein is ﴿that the earth﴾: that is, the earth of Paradise, ﴿will be inherited by My righteous servants﴾: those who performed what was commanded and avoided what was forbidden. They are the ones whom God makes inherit the Gardens, as the people of Paradise say: ﴿Praise be to God, who has guided us to this﴾, and ﴿has given us the land to inherit, to dwell in Paradise wherever we will﴾. It is also possible that what is meant is succession on earth, and that the righteous are the ones whom God establishes on earth and makes its rulers, as in His saying: ﴿God has promised those among you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will surely grant them succession upon the earth, as He granted it to those before them...﴾, the verse.

{106} Allah, exalted is He, praises His Mighty Book, the Qur'an, and shows its complete sufficiency regarding everything, and that one cannot dispense with it. He said: ﴿Indeed, in this is a message for a people who worship﴾; that is, they gain sufficiency through it in reaching their Lord and the abode of His honour. It brings them to the most exalted aims and the best desires. For the worshippers, who are the most noble of creation, there is no end beyond it, because it is the guarantor of knowing their Lord through His names, attributes and acts; of informing about true unseen matters; of calling to the realities of faith and the evidences of certainty; of clarifying all commanded and prohibited matters; of making known the defects of the soul and of deeds, and the paths that should be followed in the subtle and the major aspects of religion; and of warning against the ways of Satan and explaining his entries into man. So whoever the Qur'an does not make self-sufficient, may Allah not make him self-sufficient, and whoever it does not suffice, may Allah not suffice him.

{107} Then He praised His Messenger, who brought the Qur'an, saying: ﴿And We have not sent you except as a mercy to the worlds﴾. He is God's mercy bestowed upon His servants. Those who believe in him accepted this mercy, gave thanks for it and fulfilled its requirements, while others rejected it and ﴿replaced the favour of Allah with disbelief﴾, and refused the mercy and favour of Allah.

{108} ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad: ﴿It is only revealed to me that your God is one God﴾, who alone deserves worship. For this reason He said: ﴿Will you then submit?﴾; that is, will you submit in obedience to His servitude and surrender to His divinity? If they do, let them praise their Lord for having bestowed upon them this blessing, which surpasses all favours.

{109–110} And if they ﴿turn away﴾ from submitting to the servitude of their Lord, then warn them of the coming of exemplary punishments and the descent of retribution. ﴿Say: I have announced to you﴾; that is, I have informed you of the punishment, ﴿on equal terms﴾; that is, my knowledge and your knowledge of this are equal. So do not say, when punishment descends upon you: ''No bringer of good news or warner came to us.'' Rather, now my knowledge and your knowledge are equal, since I warned you, cautioned you and informed you of the outcome of disbelief, and I have concealed nothing from you. ﴿And I do not know whether what you are promised is near or far﴾; that is, the punishment, because its knowledge is with Allah, and it is in His hand; none of the matter is in my power.

{111} ﴿And I do not know; perhaps it is a trial for you and a provision for a time﴾; that is, perhaps the delay of the punishment you have sought hastily is an evil for you, and you will be given enjoyment in this world for a time, and then it will become a greater punishment for you.

{112} ﴿He said: My Lord, judge with truth﴾; that is, between us and the disbelieving people. Allah answered this supplication and judged between them in this world before the Hereafter, through what He punished the disbelievers with, such as the battle of Badr and others. ﴿And our Lord, the Most Merciful, is the one whose help is sought against what you describe﴾; that is, we ask our Lord, the Most Merciful, and seek His help against what you say: ''We will prevail over you, and your religion will be destroyed!'' In this we do not take pride in ourselves, nor do we rely on our own strength and power. Rather, we seek help from the Most Merciful, in whose hand is the forelock of every creature, and we hope that He will complete what we have asked of Him from His mercy. And He has done so, all praise be to Allah.

{112} ﴿He said: My Lord, judge with truth﴾; that is, between us and the disbelieving people. Allah answered this supplication and judged between them in this world before the Hereafter, through what He punished the disbelievers with, such as the battle of Badr and others. ﴿And our Lord, the Most Merciful, is the one whose help is sought against what you describe﴾; that is, we ask our Lord, the Most Merciful, and seek His help against what you say: ''We will prevail over you, and your religion will be destroyed!'' In this we do not take pride in ourselves, nor do we rely on our own strength and power. Rather, we seek help from the Most Merciful, in whose hand is the forelock of every creature, and we hope that He will complete what we have asked of Him from His mercy. And He has done so, all praise be to Allah.

{106} Allah, exalted is He, praises His Mighty Book, the Qur'an, and shows its complete sufficiency regarding everything, and that one cannot dispense with it. He said: ﴿Indeed, in this is a message for a people who worship﴾; that is, they gain sufficiency through it in reaching their Lord and the abode of His honour. It brings them to the most exalted aims and the best desires. For the worshippers, who are the most noble of creation, there is no end beyond it, because it is the guarantor of knowing their Lord through His names, attributes and acts; of informing about true unseen matters; of calling to the realities of faith and the evidences of certainty; of clarifying all commanded and prohibited matters; of making known the defects of the soul and of deeds, and the paths that should be followed in the subtle and the major aspects of religion; and of warning against the ways of Satan and explaining his entries into man. So whoever the Qur'an does not make self-sufficient, may Allah not make him self-sufficient, and whoever it does not suffice, may Allah not suffice him.

{107} Then He praised His Messenger, who brought the Qur'an, saying: ﴿And We have not sent you except as a mercy to the worlds﴾. He is God's mercy bestowed upon His servants. Those who believe in him accepted this mercy, gave thanks for it and fulfilled its requirements, while others rejected it and ﴿replaced the favour of Allah with disbelief﴾, and refused the mercy and favour of Allah.

{108} ﴿Say﴾, O Muhammad: ﴿It is only revealed to me that your God is one God﴾, who alone deserves worship. For this reason He said: ﴿Will you then submit?﴾; that is, will you submit in obedience to His servitude and surrender to His divinity? If they do, let them praise their Lord for having bestowed upon them this blessing, which surpasses all favours.

{109–110} And if they ﴿turn away﴾ from submitting to the servitude of their Lord, then warn them of the coming of exemplary punishments and the descent of retribution. ﴿Say: I have announced to you﴾; that is, I have informed you of the punishment, ﴿on equal terms﴾; that is, my knowledge and your knowledge of this are equal. So do not say, when punishment descends upon you: ''No bringer of good news or warner came to us.'' Rather, now my knowledge and your knowledge are equal, since I warned you, cautioned you and informed you of the outcome of disbelief, and I have concealed nothing from you. ﴿And I do not know whether what you are promised is near or far﴾; that is, the punishment, because its knowledge is with Allah, and it is in His hand; none of the matter is in my power.
